title: List all Namespaces and save the output
description: A DevOps team needs the list of all Namespaces in the cluster. Connect to ckad5601, list the Namespaces with kubectl, and save the output to /opt/course/1/namespaces on that instance.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad5601.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
The exact destination path /opt/course/1/namespaces must be used.
Do not create, edit or delete any cluster objects.

commands.purpose: Open a session on the exam instance (simulated).
List every Namespace and redirect stdout into the required file.

commands.expectedStdout:
NAME              STATUS   AGE
default           Active   44d
kube-node-lease   Active   44d
kube-public       Active   44d
kube-system       Active   44d

artifacts.description: File containing the full Namespace listing.
artifacts.content:
NAME              STATUS   AGE
default           Active   44d
kube-node-lease   Active   44d
kube-public       Active   44d
kube-system       Active   44d

successCriteria: Connected to ckad5601 in the simulated session.
The file contains the complete Namespace table with a NAME, STATUS and AGE column.
rationale: kubectl get namespaces (alias: kubectl get ns) is a read-only, cluster-scoped command, so it works from any namespace without extra permissions. Shell redirection with > captures stdout into a file on the instance where the command runs. The exam checks the resulting file, not the route you took, so the exact path matters more than the alias used.
referenceNotes: Documentation: kubectl get namespaces returns all Namespace objects; it is cluster-scoped and does not require -n.
Aliases: kubectl get ns, kubectl get namespace and kubectl get namespaces are equivalent.
Redirection: > writes (or truncates) a file; >> appends. A fresh file is required here.
Exam tip: verify with cat before finishing, because a typo in the path creates the wrong file.
